name: Atlantic Coast Conference
prestige: Elite — #1 men's soccer conference nationally
mlsPipeline: Highest in college soccer — leads all conferences in MLS picks 2020–2026
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies split across roster — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The most prestigious men's soccer conference in the United States. Virginia holds 7 national titles. Clemson won in 2021 and 2023. Maryland under Cirovski is the all-time MLS picks leader. ACC has produced more MLS #1 overall draft picks than any other conference in the past decade. The competition level is equivalent to a top European second division in terms of athleticism and tactical sophistication.
olivierNote: 13 guide schools in the ACC — the most of any conference. Clemson (Noonan, 2× champion) is the #1 pipeline program nationally. SMU won the 2025 ACC Tournament (first ever). Virginia 7× champions. UNC ACC Regular Season champs 2023. Notre Dame 27 MLS picks. Stanford and Cal add West Coast depth. All 13 are viable targets depending on Olivier's profile level.

name: Big Ten Conference
prestige: Elite — #2 overall, dominant Midwest and West
mlsPipeline: Top 5 — Indiana all-time leader; Maryland most all-time picks; UCLA strong West Coast pipeline
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The Big Ten expanded to include West Coast powerhouses UCLA and USC in 2024. Indiana is the most decorated men's soccer program in US history (8 NCAA titles). UCLA joins as a 4-time national champion. Maryland has produced the most MLS picks of any college program all-time (49 + 7 homegrown under Cirovski). The conference now spans both coasts.
olivierNote: All 14 Big Ten schools now fully profiled. Indiana and UCLA are the historical elite. Maryland under Cirovski is the all-time MLS pipeline leader. UCLA (LA lifestyle, 4 national titles) is the closest Big Ten match to Olivier's Sydney background. Penn State, Michigan, Ohio State, and USC are the next tier. Washington (Seattle) and Oregon (Eugene) add Pacific Northwest options. Rutgers and Northwestern are the most accessible GPA entry points.

name: Big East Conference
prestige: Very Strong — #3-4 nationally, NYC-anchored
mlsPipeline: Strong — Georgetown 42 MLS signings under Wiese. Multiple Red Bulls/NYCFC connections from St John's.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: Akron (Akron, OH) — joined for men's soccer in 2023; won the Big East Midwest Division in 2024 & 2025
desc: The Big East features many urban campuses across the East Coast, making it culturally diverse and clinically connected for students targeting health careers. Georgetown won the 2019 national championship under Brian Wiese. St. John's in Queens NYC has access to the Hospital for Special Surgery — the #1 orthopaedic hospital in the world. Creighton in Omaha is consistently top-10 nationally.
olivierNote: All 11 Big East schools now fully profiled. Georgetown (2019 champion, 42 MLS signings) and St. John's (NYC, Hospital for Special Surgery access) remain the top Olivier targets. Creighton is consistently top-10 nationally. UConn under Ray Reid is the strongest program in the Northeast. Big East is extremely competitive — strong highlights required. Marquette (Milwaukee) and Butler (Indianapolis) are the most accessible entry points for international recruits. Akron is a Big East men's-soccer affiliate from 2023 (its other sports remain in the MAC) — a top-20 MLS pipeline and the best Pre-PT value in the guide.

name: Southeastern Conference
prestige: Elite academic + athletic brand. Men's soccer at selected schools only.
mlsPipeline: Growing — Texas A&M consistent SEC producer. Gyasi Zardes (Columbus Crew, USMNT) most famous alum.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: ⚠ UF — academic reference only (no men's varsity)
desc: The SEC sponsors men's soccer at only some member schools. Texas A&M is the guide's fully-profiled SEC program — Bobby Shuttleworth was appointed in December 2025 bringing a 2× national championship pedigree from Florida State. Texas A&M has one of the largest kinesiology departments in the US (~3,000 undergrads). UF is retained as an academic reference only — no men's varsity soccer.
olivierNote: Texas A&M is the SEC pick — massive kinesiology department, Shuttleworth's championship pedigree, warm climate. College Station is a college town not a major city. Trade-off: lifestyle vs elite academic/soccer development. Worth a contact email from Platform Sports Management.

name: American Athletic Conference
prestige: Very Strong — #5-6 nationally, rising fast
mlsPipeline: Strong and growing — FIU and USF are consistent MLS producers. FAU 2025 AAC Tournament Champions.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The American Athletic Conference has emerged as a genuine high-major conference in soccer. FIU reached the AAC Championship Final in 2024 and 2025. FAU won the 2025 AAC Tournament. USF rebuilding under Kiefer (second tenure). The conference offers warm-climate campuses, strong exercise science degrees, and accessible D1 competition.
olivierNote: 13 guide schools in the AAC — the most complete AAC coverage in the guide. Florida trio (FIU, USF, FAU) are Olivier's top AAC fits — warm climate, accessible GPA, strong exercise science. FAU has the best explicit Pre-PT degree. FIU has the Inter Miami pipeline. Charlotte is the rising program (No.24 nationally 2025). Rice is the academic standout (Texas Medical Center adjacent). Navy and Army are listed for completeness — service commitment incompatible with DPT/MLS goals.

name: Big West Conference
prestige: Strong — dominant West Coast regional conference
mlsPipeline: Solid — Manu Duah #1 overall 2025 is the marquee recent example
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The Big West is the premier West Coast conference below the Big Ten. UCSB under Tim Vom Steeg (20+ year coach) produced Manu Duah as the #1 overall 2025 MLS pick — the highest ever Big West draft selection. Pacific coastal lifestyle makes Big West schools lifestyle matches for Sydney-raised players.
olivierNote: UCSB is the Big West pick — Vom Steeg is the most experienced coach in the guide, Mediterranean campus, and Manu Duah #1 overall 2025. The kinesiology degree is strong and the Santa Barbara lifestyle is the closest thing to Sydney in the US.

name: Ivy League
prestige: Academic elite — no athletic scholarships
mlsPipeline: Growing — Princeton 5 MLS players under Barlow. Kevin O'Toole (NYCFC 2022) most recent.
scholarships: ZERO athletic scholarships — need-based financial aid only
desc: The Ivy League offers need-based financial aid that can cover 100% of costs for qualifying families — but zero athletic scholarships. Princeton won the 2024 AND 2025 Ivy League Tournaments under Jim Barlow — the first program ever to win both the league and tournament in back-to-back years. Yale won in 2023. Admission requires 3.9+ GPA.
olivierNote: Princeton is surging — Jim Barlow has explicitly developed midfielders into MLS-calibre players. If Olivier's GPA climbs to 3.5+, a Princeton contact email through Platform Sports Management is worth attempting. The Ivy brand enormously enhances DPT school applications. No athletic scholarships is the critical barrier.

name: Colonial Athletic Association
prestige: Competitive mid-major — East Coast D1
mlsPipeline: Developing — Charleston Battery (USL) connection is the pro draw
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The CAA is a mid-major D1 conference spanning the East Coast. It now includes 8 fully-profiled guide schools — among the most diverse conference coverage in the guide. Hofstra has won 4 consecutive CAA Tournament titles (2022-25) and earned a No.7 NCAA seed in 2024. Elon won the 2022 and 2025 CAA titles. Charleston's Keith Wiggans (Battery USL connection) is building steadily. Delaware left the CAA in 2025 — its men's soccer now competes in the Summit League (filed separately in this guide).
olivierNote: 8 CAA guide schools with full profiles. Hofstra is the dominant program — 4 consecutive titles, NYC access via LIRR, best development environment in the conference. Northeastern (Boston co-op clinical) and Drexel (Philly co-op) offer the best pre-PT pathways. Stony Brook has the best cost-to-clinical-access ratio (Stony Brook Medicine on campus, SUNY pricing). Charleston remains the only warm-climate CAA pick.

name: ASUN Conference
prestige: Developing mid-major — South and Southeast
mlsPipeline: Limited — USL League One/Two connections building at UCA
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The ASUN Conference is a mid-major D1 conference spanning the South and Southeast. UCA in Conway AR is 20 minutes from Little Rock — warm climate, affordable living, and a strong Kinesiology department with UAMS clinical network access. 6 of UCA's 9 midfielders clear before Olivier arrives — the most open central midfielder opportunity of any D1 in the guide.
olivierNote: UCA is the best value D1 in the guide — ~$28k/yr, warm climate, best MF opening of any D1, UAMS clinical network for pre-PT. Coach Segebart has an internationally diverse roster. Conway/Little Rock is not a coastal city but it's warm and affordable.

name: Western Athletic Conference
prestige: Growing mid-major — GCU 2025 Sweet 16 run elevated the conference
mlsPipeline: Developing — Dayne St. Clair (Minnesota United, USMNT) most famous WAC alum. GCU pipeline growing.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The WAC is a growing mid-major conference with teams primarily in the Southwest. GCU's 2025 run to the NCAA Sweet 16 (beating UCLA and San Diego) was the program's most historic achievement. Jamie Davies was appointed December 2025 — bringing an elite turnaround record from UNF. GCU's Phoenix campus is exceptional: 28,000 students, world-class facilities, warm climate, Banner Health clinical network.
olivierNote: GCU is the best warm D1 city campus outside Florida and California. Phoenix gives Olivier the closest climate to Sydney of any non-coastal US city. Davies has a proven record of rapid program building. Kinesiology + Banner Health = legitimate pre-PT pathway.

name: West Coast Conference
prestige: Strong mid-major — Denver joining 2026 elevates the conference
mlsPipeline: Growing — Denver is the dominant new member. Cole Bassett (Colorado Rapids, USMNT) most famous recent alum.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: Denver — University of Denver (fully profiled, joining WCC 2026)
desc: The West Coast Conference is a respected mid-major conference with strong academic institutions. Denver joins in 2026 — the most significant addition to WCC men's soccer in years. Denver's 5 consecutive Summit League titles and 2024 College Cup appearance makes them an immediate WCC contender. Jamie Franks is one of the most technically precise coaches in D1.
olivierNote: Denver is the WCC pick — 5 titles, College Cup 2024, outstanding Denver city lifestyle, and Franks is underrated. Kinesiology degree launched 2023 but NSCA-certified. Moving to WCC means stronger competition from 2026. Cold winters are the trade-off.

name: America East Conference
prestige: Mid-major — Vermont's 2024 national championship shocked the soccer world
mlsPipeline: Developing — Vermont's 2024 championship launched Kissel and Papp into MLS. Growing pipeline.
scholarships: Up to 9.9 athletic equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
desc: The America East gained national attention when Vermont won the 2024 NCAA Championship — beating Marshall 2-1 in OT with a dramatic golden goal from Maximilian Kissel. Rob Dow built one of the most passionate soccer cultures in college sport. New coach Adrian Dubois in 2026. Burlington is cold but the soccer tradition is now elite.
olivierNote: Vermont is listed depth only — the climate and lifestyle are not a match for Olivier. The 2024 national championship is historic and program momentum under Dubois is worth monitoring. Not a priority target but worth awareness.

name: Sunshine State Conference
prestige: #1 D2 conference nationally — dominates national rankings
mlsPipeline: Best non-MLS pipeline — USL2, international pro signings annually from multiple SSC teams
scholarships: Up to 9 athletic equivalencies (D2 maximum)
desc: The Sunshine State Conference is consistently ranked as the top Division II conference in men's soccer nationally. PBA finished ranked #2 nationally in 2025. Barry has 4 all-time national championships. Lynn are the 2024 D2 national champions (20-0-2 undefeated). The entire conference is in South Florida — warm, coastal, and diverse.
olivierNote: The SSC is arguably the single best conference for Olivier's overall needs. 4 guide schools all in warm Florida cities within 60 minutes of each other. PBA is #2 nationally with Pre-PT in the degree title. Barry has the most D2 titles ever. Lynn 2024 champions. Nova SE has its own DPT program.

name: Lone Star Conference
prestige: Strong regional — Texas and Oklahoma
mlsPipeline: Developing — Austin FC (MLS) connections via St Edward's proximity
scholarships: Up to 9 athletic equivalencies
desc: The Lone Star Conference covers Texas and Oklahoma in Division II. St. Edward's in Austin is the flagship LSC soccer program, with Brian Young's possession-based attacking style producing consistent LSC Championship contenders. Austin FC (MLS) is headquartered nearby, creating a genuine professional pathway.
olivierNote: St. Edward's is the best Texas pick for Olivier. Brian Young's European pressing system is perfect for an 8/10 midfielder. Austin is warm, urban, and culturally dynamic. Austin FC pipeline is a rare MLS-affiliated pro pathway at D2 level.

name: California Collegiate Athletic Association
prestige: Competitive West Coast D2
mlsPipeline: Limited MLS; strong sport science career placement in LA
scholarships: Up to 9 athletic equivalencies
desc: The CCAA is the West Coast Division II conference featuring California State University system schools. Cal State LA has a dedicated School of Kinesiology and Nutritional Science. LA location means unparalleled clinical access and career placement in sports medicine and physical therapy.
olivierNote: Cal State LA is the most affordable LA option at ~$28k/yr. The kinesiology program is strong and the LA clinical network for pre-PT is outstanding. Not the most competitive soccer but the lifestyle and academic value are excellent.

name: Mountain East Conference
prestige: Regional D2 — Appalachian region
mlsPipeline: Limited — USL pathway developing. UC Charleston has Australian connection (Jack Allan).
scholarships: Up to 9 athletic equivalencies
desc: The Mountain East Conference covers West Virginia and the Mid-Atlantic in Division II. UC Charleston's CAMC hospital clinical partnership gives pre-PT students a legitimate clinical placement pathway. Jack Allan from Cape Schanck, Victoria is currently on UC Charleston's roster — a confirmed Australian recruiting connection.
olivierNote: UC Charleston is notable primarily for two reasons: Jack Allan (AUS) on the current roster confirms international recruiting, and the CAMC hospital partnership is a genuine pre-PT clinical pathway. Not a lifestyle match for Olivier but a viable option if other doors close.

name: Sooner Athletic Conference
prestige: Strong NAIA — Oklahoma City University tradition
mlsPipeline: NAIA level — semi-pro and international pathways
scholarships: Up to equivalent of full ride (NAIA)
desc: The Sooner Athletic Conference is a competitive NAIA conference in the South Central region. Oklahoma City University has a strong soccer tradition built by founder coach Brian Harvey (NAIA Hall of Fame) who played professionally in Australia. Billy Martin took over in 2020 continuing that legacy. NAIA is more generous than the NCAA at 12 equivalencies, and with no per-player cap a full ride is possible — though the team total is still capped.
olivierNote: OCU is the NAIA pick — Brian Finnegan's historical Australian connections, generous scholarships, warm Oklahoma City. Not a major coastal city lifestyle but solid soccer development and strong kinesiology pathway.

name: Sun Conference
prestige: Strong Florida NAIA — Keiser health sciences focus
mlsPipeline: Limited — health sciences pathway is the priority
scholarships: Up to equivalent of full ride (NAIA)
desc: The Sun Conference is a NAIA conference primarily in Florida. Keiser University is primarily a health sciences institution — the Clinical Simulation Centre at Keiser provides hands-on patient care simulation before graduate school, which is extremely rare at undergraduate level.
olivierNote: Keiser is the right choice if PT/Chiro pathway is the absolute priority over soccer profile. West Palm Beach warm and cosmopolitan, with Fort Lauderdale 45 minutes south. Clinical Simulation Centre gives pre-grad experience unavailable at most US programs.

name: Southern CA Intercollegiate Athletic Conference
prestige: Strong D3 — best D3 conference in California
mlsPipeline: None (D3) — academic/PT pathway focus
scholarships: ZERO athletic scholarships — merit and need-based aid only
desc: SCIAC is the premier Division III conference in Southern California. Chapman University's KIN 405 Pre-Physical Therapy Prep is a required course — the only program in the guide with this mandatory pre-PT preparation. Orange County clinical network (Hoag Hospital, CHOC) provides excellent DPT observation hours.
olivierNote: Chapman D3 = less schedule pressure = better GPA performance for PT grad school applications. No athletic scholarships but merit aid and the Hoag Hospital clinical network are strong compensators. Orange County is 30 minutes from LA.

prestige: Transfer pathway — not a career destination
mlsPipeline: Pathway — SMC → UCLA transfer pipeline is the most proven in California
scholarships: Athletic grants + need-based aid (varies by state)

desc: Community college and junior college programs serve as 2-year transfer platforms. 70 guide schools now span 13 NJCAA regions represented in the guide (Region 1 AZ/NV/CA, Region 2 OK/AR, Region 4 IL, Region 5 TX, Region 6 KS, Region 8 FL, Region 9 CO/WY/NE, Region 10 SC, Region 11 IA/NE, Region 14 TX/LA, Region 15 NY, Region 20 MD, Region 24 IL), plus Santa Monica College (CCCAA, non-NJCAA). Region 10 (South Carolina) makes its guide debut with all four of the region's DI schools that share a conference bracket: USC Lancaster, USC Salkehatchie, USC Sumter and USC Union — a fifth DI-listed school, Denmark Technical College, was found to have moved its soccer program to the USCAA (a separate national governing body) for 2025-26 and was excluded, the same class of finding as Batch 6's Pratt CC. USC Lancaster won the 2025 Region 10 DI Tournament as the No. 3 seed (upsetting both USC Sumter and USC Union) and reached the NJCAA Southeast District Final. USC Sumter was the 2024-25 Region 10 regular-season champion (10-1-2). USC Union posted the program's best-ever season in 2025-26 (Region 10 regular-season champion, 10-2-4) and has produced the Region 10 DI Player of the Year four years running. USC Salkehatchie, in on-field decline, carries the region's longest-tenured coach (William Glass, 16th season) and real 2025-26 academic honors. None of the four USC regional campuses offers a dedicated Exercise Science or Kinesiology credential — all four are limited to the general-transfer Associate in Arts/Science — and none has on-campus dormitories. Region 9 grows to ten guide schools alongside Otero College: Casper College, Northwest College, Central Wyoming College, Laramie County Community College and Gillette College (all Wyoming), plus Western Nebraska Community College, Lamar Community College, Trinidad State College and Northeastern Junior College (Colorado/Nebraska) join the region. Western Nebraska CC won the 2024 Region IX title and made the program's first-ever NJCAA DI National Tournament appearance, producing WNCC's first-ever NJCAA All-American (Eduardo Oliveira) — all at the batch's cheapest cost of attendance ($14,125/yr). Trinidad State's program-alumnus head coach Tyler Wilt returned in 2025 after four years as head coach at York University (NE). Northeastern Junior College's 2025-26 midfield group clears entirely before 2027 under Interim HC Hubert Blanco. Lamar CC pairs a genuine Athletic Training Practicum clinical sequence with new head coach Alieu Kamara, owner of a professional academy in Guinea. Laramie County Community College's own team account credits the program with 11 NJCAA DI Region IX titles and 3 National Tournament appearances across its history, independently Tier-1 confirmed for a 2018 Region IX title and National Tournament run beating Region 10 Champion Seminole State. Casper College and Northwest College met in the 2025 Region 9 semifinal (Northwest won 1-0 on the road), with Casper going on to two confirmed 2025 NJCAA All-Americans and Northwest advancing to the Region 9 final under UEFA 'B'-licensed head coach Rob Hill. Region 6 (Kansas) grows to five guide schools alongside Cowley, Barton, Dodge City and Neosho County: Coffeyville Community College was named NJCAA Academic Team of the Year for men's soccer in 2025-26 (3.85 team GPA, #1 nationally) under veteran five-program head coach Steven Harrison; Garden City Community College's 2025 season was officially billed by the college as 'one of the most successful in program history' under alumnus head coach Oscar Zelaya, who played on Garden City's own 2008 NJCAA DI National Tournament 4th-place team before a 7-year Dodge City CC head-coaching stint; and Seward County Community College is one of the youngest programs in the guide (launched fall 2023) under founding head coach Jaime Beltran, who led Ranger College to its first-ever NJCAA DI Region 5 Championship and National Tournament berth in 2013. Harry S. Truman College (Chicago, IL) is the NJCAA Region 4 Division I Champion three consecutive seasons (2023-2025) under three-time Region 4 Coach of the Year Maciej Orlowski — the strongest sustained regional dominance found anywhere in this campaign outside a national title. Richard J. Daley, Malcolm X, Kennedy-King and Wilbur Wright Colleges round out Region 4's five City Colleges of Chicago guide schools — all NJCAA Division I, all commuter campuses in Chicago proper with zero on-campus housing anywhere in the CCC system, and all sharing one district-wide tuition schedule. Phoenix College (Phoenix, AZ) are the 2025 NJCAA DII National Champions, ranked #1 nationally for 7 straight weeks. Indian Hills CC (Ottumwa, IA) are the 2025 NJCAA DI National Champions under Zac Newton. Daytona State College (Daytona Beach, FL) were the 2025 NJCAA DI finalists — top-5 D1 transfer feeder, warm Florida lifestyle. Tyler Junior College (Tyler, TX) is the #1 JUCO D1 transfer feeder nationally. Monroe University Mustangs (New Rochelle, NY) are 3× NJCAA DI National Champions with Australian alumni on roster. Santa Monica College (Santa Monica, CA) has the best documented transfer pipeline to UCLA in California at ~$9k/yr. Suffolk County CC (Selden, NY) won the 2025 NJCAA Region 15 Division III Championship — Region 15's only Division I program is Monroe University (New Rochelle); Suffolk, Nassau, Ulster County and Westchester all compete at Division III (corrected 2026-08-11; Division III cannot offer athletic scholarships under NJCAA rules). Arizona Western College is ranked #2 nationally (2025) with a genuine Exercise, Wellness and Nutrition degree. Eastern Florida State plays in a 1,000-seat stadium-grade facility with back-to-back national tournament runs. Otero College (La Junta, CO) and Montgomery College (Rockville, MD) both won their 2025 NJCAA DI Region/District titles and won a match at the 2025 National Tournament. Yavapai College (Prescott, AZ) is a seven-time national champion program that reached the 2025 Region 1 Championship final. College of Southern Nevada (Las Vegas, NV) is the guide's only JUCO in a genuine major city, with the deepest sports-medicine staffing in this Region 1 group. Region 2 (Oklahoma/Arkansas) now has seven guide schools alongside Murray State College: Eastern Oklahoma State, Connors State, Northeastern Oklahoma A&M, Rose State, National Park College, and University of Arkansas Rich Mountain — the latter two Arkansas-based and playing a smaller cross-state conference pool within the same region. Region 5 (Texas) makes its guide debut with Hill College and Western Texas College, who met in the 2025 Region 5 Tournament Final. Region 14 (Texas) makes its guide debut with four schools that share one conference bracket in East/South Texas: Paris Junior College, Jacksonville College, Northeast Texas Community College, and Texas Southmost College. None carries a Region 14 title or postseason result in this campaign's 2021-2025 research window, and all four are genuinely modest on-field programs, but each has a real distinguishing story. Paris JC's transfer pipeline is growing fast under head coach Fernando Arellano (a former NCAA D1 player, NJCAA All-American, and Liga MX professional): a program-record 10 players signed to continue their careers in June 2026, up from 7 the year before, including back-to-back NCAA Division I transfers (Houston Christian 2025, Missouri State 2026). Northeast Texas CC's head coach Jon Evan carries one of the deepest individually-documented CVs in this entire campaign — assistant roles at two different NCAA Division I programs (including directly developing a future MLS SuperDraft pick), an NCAA D2 head-coaching conference title, and two separate NCAA D3 head-coaching program-best tenures — even though the program itself, in an early rebuild since his April 2023 hire, currently carries Region 14's weakest on-field record. Jacksonville College is the smallest school in this entire campaign (~550 students, a private Christian junior college) with a genuinely large, wide-open midfield pool heading into 2026-27. Texas Southmost College is the campaign's newest confirmed program — launched NJCAA competition in 2023-24 under founding head coach and TSC/UTB alumnus Mario Zamora, who holds a genuine binational Mexican FA (FMF) and US Soccer coaching license — and is the only school in this batch on a real city campus (Brownsville, on the US-Mexico border), though it has no on-campus housing anywhere in the TSC system, unlike Paris JC, Jacksonville, and Northeast Texas CC, which all offer real on-campus dorms.
olivierNote: Harry S. Truman College (Chicago, IL) is the strongest on-field program added to the guide this session — an NJCAA Region 4 Division I three-peat champion (2023-2025) under a three-time Region 4 Coach of the Year — but Chicago's cold winters (not a warm-climate match) hold its Fit Score below the guide's Sun Belt JUCOs despite the results. Richard J. Daley College shows the clearest coaching-driven turnaround of this batch (1-11-3 to 8-6 across three seasons) under a UK-educated part-time coach. Malcolm X College is the only one of the five Chicago City Colleges with a genuine on-campus exercise-science program — a Personal Fitness Trainer certificate at CCC's $251M Health Sciences center — under the longest-tenured coach in the batch (since 2014). Kennedy-King and Wilbur Wright are both still-developing programs (Wright freshly funded by a 2026 NJCAA Foundation grant); all five share one Chicago-wide reality: a major-city lifestyle match offset by zero on-campus housing anywhere in the City Colleges of Chicago district. Phoenix College is now the guide's most decorated current JUCO — 2025 national champions, warm major-city Arizona campus, confirmed dedicated Exercise Science degree. Indian Hills is the DI national champion — elite performance play, cold rural Iowa. Daytona State is the best lifestyle JUCO — warm Florida beach city, 2025 national finalist, top-5 D1 transfer feeder. Tyler JC is the #1 D1 transfer record nationally — warm East Texas city, and was beaten by Montgomery College at the 2025 National Tournament. Monroe is NYC metro lifestyle with 3× NJCAA DI titles at the New Rochelle campus — its Bronx campus fields a separate NJCAA Division III team and is not in this guide. Suffolk County CC (also NYC metro, 2025 Region 15 Division III champions) is the only Lower New York JUCO with a confirmed dedicated Exercise Science degree, but as a Division III program it cannot offer athletic scholarships (corrected 2026-08-11) — the same applies to Nassau, Ulster County and Westchester, the guide's other three Region 15 schools. Santa Monica is the Sydney-lifestyle match — ocean, LA culture, → UCLA pipeline. Arizona Western pairs a #2 national ranking with warm desert climate and a real Exercise/Wellness/Nutrition degree. Eastern Florida State has the best dedicated soccer stadium (1,000 seats) among guide JUCOs plus warm Space Coast lifestyle. Cowley, Barton, Dodge City, and Neosho County (all Kansas) are nationally ranked but a poor climate fit; Johnson County CC (Overland Park, KS) offers the same conference at a genuine Kansas City metro campus. Lewis & Clark Community College (Godfrey, IL, Region 24) has the guide's deepest JUCO coaching CV — head coach John Dunn has built three different programs into conference/regional winners — plus a genuine dedicated Exercise Science degree, offset by a cold-winter Midwest setting with no on-campus housing. Murray State College (Tishomingo, OK) is the guide's most freshman-open JUCO: all 17 freshmen on the 2026-27 roster entered from high school with no JUCO or 4-year transfers, and the squad includes an Australian from Sydney. Back-to-back National Tournament qualifiers at roughly $18.5k/yr — the trade-off is a remote rural campus and no strength & conditioning staff. Otero College (La Junta, CO) is the guide's most in-form JUCO on results — a 2025 Region/Tournament/District sweep, Otero's first-ever national tournament win, and a record-breaking 13-player transfer class — offset by a rural, cold-winter Colorado setting with no dedicated Exercise Science degree. Montgomery College (Rockville, MD) pairs one of the guide's most credentialed coaches (USSF 'B'/UEFA C-licensed Pedro Braz) and a CAAHEP-accredited Exercise Science degree with genuine DC-metro access, offset by zero on-campus housing and a high cost of living. Yavapai College (Prescott, AZ) carries the deepest historical prestige in the Arizona group — seven national titles — and reached the 2025 Region 1 final under a new internationally-experienced head coach, offset by a cool mountain climate unlike the rest of Arizona's JUCOs. Eastern Arizona College (Thatcher, AZ) is the guide's newest program (launched 2023) and already a Region 1 semifinalist, with a genuinely PT-relevant Sports Medicine Professions degree, in a small remote Gila Valley town. College of Southern Nevada (Las Vegas, NV) is the only JUCO in this batch set in a real major city — a close lifestyle match for a Sydney athlete — backed by a fully accredited Physical Therapist Assistant AAS and the deepest sports-medicine staffing of the group, offset by zero on-campus housing anywhere in the CSN system and the highest cost in the batch. Community Christian College (San Bernardino, CA) is a structurally unusual, multi-state online-first college fielding a winless ACCAC team with minimal academic and coaching infrastructure — treat with caution. Eastern Oklahoma State College (Wilburton, OK) is the most consistently competitive of the four new Region 2 Oklahoma schools — three straight Region 2/South District postseason finals (2023-2025), all three losses coming to Murray State College, under a head coach with a genuine multi-title CV from outside the NJCAA system. Rose State College (Midwest City, OK) is the strongest overall package of the four: genuine Oklahoma City metro access (the only city-lifestyle match among Region 2's five guide schools), the best-resourced athletics department, and the guide's best Region-2 academic fit — a real Exercise/Fitness Management degree including an actual Physiology of Exercise course — offset by mid-table on-field results. Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College (Miami, OK) backs two solid recent seasons with the best-staffed athletic training department of the four, though its interim head coach was named just one day before this research. Connors State College (Warner, OK) is the youngest program in the guide (est. 2023) and has already reached the Region 2 Tournament every season, but its head coaching position is genuinely vacant as of this research — a national search is underway after founding coach Adam Skolnick departed for MLS Next in April 2026. 53 guide schools — all 2-year transfer platforms. National Park College (Hot Springs, AR) is the guide's newest men's soccer program (founded January 2024) and already produced the best 2025-26 raw win total of this batch (8-4-3), in a genuine Arkansas resort town, offset by the thinnest coaching staff and facility footprint researched this session — no assistant coach, no dedicated home venue. University of Arkansas Rich Mountain (Mena, AR) carries real historical Region 2 prestige (outright champions in 2019 and 2021) and now fields the guide's most extensively credentialed JUCO head coach on paper — five prior head-coaching stints including four NCAA D1 programs — in a small, quiet Ouachita Mountains town. Hill College (Hillsboro, TX) is this batch's standout turnaround story: winless in conference play in 2024 to Region 5 regular-season champions and Tournament Finalists in 2025 under first-year head coach and program alumnus Ivan Franco (2025 Region 5 Coach of the Year), backed by the guide's most directly DPT-titled academic pathway (a genuine Pre-Physical Therapy A.S.) and by far the lowest cost in this batch at $9,390/yr. Western Texas College (Snyder, TX) delivered the best confirmed 2025 postseason result of the batch — Region 5 Tournament Champions, then NJCAA Mid-South District runner-up to eventual national qualifier Murray State — backed by the only officially confirmed dedicated soccer complex and fitness center in this group, under a first-year head coach with an unusual pro-club scouting/data-analytics pedigree. Coffeyville Community College (Coffeyville, KS) pairs a genuinely dedicated Athletic Training AS degree with a supervised clinical practicum with head coach Steven Harrison's 15-year, five-program JUCO résumé, and was separately named the NJCAA's #1 academically-ranked men's soccer team nationally for 2025-26 — a real strength offset by mid-table KJCCC results since Harrison's 2023 arrival. Garden City Community College (Garden City, KS) is led by a genuine program alumnus, Oscar Zelaya, who played on the school's own #4-nationally-ranked 2008 national-tournament team before a 7-year Dodge City CC head-coaching stint (KJCCC West Coach of the Year 2019); 2025 was officially billed as 'one of the most successful seasons in program history,' backed by a named Sterling University Pre-Athletic Training articulation. Seward County Community College (Liberal, KS) is the youngest program in this Region 6 group (launched fall 2023) under founding head coach Jaime Beltran, whose ~20-year CV includes leading Ranger College to its first-ever NJCAA DI Region 5 Championship and National Tournament berth (2013); the young program delivered a first-ever playoff berth in its 2023 debut season and a 2025-26 NJCAA Academic Team of the Year honor for men's soccer, offset by a steep on-field decline in 2025 (winless in conference) and a shared, off-campus home venue. Laramie County Community College (Cheyenne, WY) pairs the campaign's strongest ACU-aligned JUCO degree — a Kinesiology & Health Promotion A.S. with a required internship — with a historically dominant program (11X Region IX Champions per the team's own account) and a brand-new $31M athletics complex featuring a dedicated soccer field and a hospital-partnered fitness center, offset by a real, honestly-disclosed pipeline gap: zero confirmed NCAA Division I soccer placements across more than two decades of the program's own recorded alumni history (NCAA D2/NAIA-weighted instead). Casper College's standout asset is a genuinely deep and sustained NCAA transfer pipeline under program-founder head coach Ben McArthur — 19 movers across the last two off-seasons, 5 to NCAA Division I, including two 2025 NJCAA All-Americans — offset by the program having no dedicated on-campus soccer stadium as of the 2025-26 season. Northwest College (Powell, WY) is led by head coach Rob Hill, whose UEFA 'B' License and United Coaches Master Coach Diploma are the deepest coaching credentials found anywhere in this campaign, immediately returning the program to a 2025 Region 9 final on his return after a 4-year absence. Gillette College pairs a genuinely dedicated Exercise Science A.S. with real recent facility investment — a purpose-built soccer field (2020) and an $18.5M academic-athletic complex with a health simulation lab — under a first-time Wyoming-native head coach and a still-establishing program. Central Wyoming College (Riverton, WY) is the most modest profile of this Wyoming group: a program in an early rebuilding phase under a first-season head coach, with no dedicated Kinesiology or Exercise Science degree. Western Nebraska CC (Scottsbluff, NE) is the strongest recent-history story of this Region 9 batch — a first-ever 2024 Region IX title, first-ever NJCAA DI National Tournament appearance, and the program's first-ever NJCAA All-American (Eduardo Oliveira) — under 20-plus-year HC Todd Rasnic, who then handed the reins to his own longtime assistant and WNCC alumnus Eseah Ingram for a 2025-26 rebuild season; also the cheapest cost of attendance added anywhere in this campaign ($14,125/yr). Trinidad State College (Trinidad, CO) is a program genuinely mid-rebuild under returning alumnus HC Tyler Wilt (four years as head coach at York University, NE), with a thin, all-freshman 2025-26 midfield (3 total) meaning a wide-open Minutes Outlook, and the guide's only named, direct AA-to-BS Exercise Science transfer agreement (with CSU Pueblo). Northeastern Junior College (Sterling, CO) had its best recent season in 2022 (3rd of 9 Region 9) and carries this batch's strongest-branded Athletic Training pathway with real clinical practicum hours, under Interim HC Hubert Blanco — a substantive 7-year high-school/club coaching CV despite the interim title — with a fully-cleared 7-player 2025-26 midfield group. Lamar Community College (Lamar, CO) is this batch's clearest results-vs-academics trade-off: the region's weakest on-field record (a combined 3-31-1 in Region 9 conference play across four seasons) under brand-new HC Alieu Kamara (owner of a professional academy in Guinea, his first head-coaching role), offset by a genuine Athletic Training Practicum clinical sequence and a discounted international-student tuition pilot rate. Region 10 (South Carolina) debuts with USC Lancaster, USC Salkehatchie, USC Sumter and USC Union — four University of South Carolina regional campuses that play each other in one shared conference bracket. USC Lancaster is the most recently in-form: 2025 Region 10 DI Tournament Champion as the No. 3 seed (beating both USC Sumter and USC Union in the same run) and NJCAA Southeast District Runner-up, under six-year dual men's/women's head coach Kenny Halas. USC Sumter's case rests on the 2024-25 Region 10 regular-season title (10-1-2, the best record of any Region 10 school in this window) and first-year head coach Adam Howarth, whose NCAA D1/D2/D3 and professional playing CV is one of the deepest found anywhere in this campaign. USC Union is this batch's standout individual-development story — four consecutive Region 10 DI Players of the Year (2022-2025) under 2x Coach of the Year Marc Curlee, capped by the program's best-ever 2025-26 season — though its home field is an off-campus municipal facility, not on campus. USC Salkehatchie is the region's clearest opportunity play: a wide-open midfield (all four current midfielders clear before Olivier's August 2027 arrival) under William Glass, one of the longest-tenured coaches in this whole campaign (16th season, 218-186-24 career record), offsetting a program in real on-field decline. All four USC campuses share the same structural trade-off: no dedicated Exercise Science/Kinesiology credential at the two-year level, and no on-campus housing anywhere in the system. Region 14 (Texas) makes its guide debut with four schools that share one conference bracket in East/South Texas: Paris Junior College, Jacksonville College, Northeast Texas Community College, and Texas Southmost College. None carries a Region 14 title or postseason result in this campaign's 2021-2025 research window, and all four are genuinely modest on-field programs, but each has a real distinguishing story. Paris JC's transfer pipeline is growing fast under head coach Fernando Arellano (a former NCAA D1 player, NJCAA All-American, and Liga MX professional): a program-record 10 players signed to continue their careers in June 2026, up from 7 the year before, including back-to-back NCAA Division I transfers (Houston Christian 2025, Missouri State 2026). Northeast Texas CC's head coach Jon Evan carries one of the deepest individually-documented CVs in this entire campaign — assistant roles at two different NCAA Division I programs (including directly developing a future MLS SuperDraft pick), an NCAA D2 head-coaching conference title, and two separate NCAA D3 head-coaching program-best tenures — even though the program itself, in an early rebuild since his April 2023 hire, currently carries Region 14's weakest on-field record. Jacksonville College is the smallest school in this entire campaign (~550 students, a private Christian junior college) with a genuinely large, wide-open midfield pool heading into 2026-27. Texas Southmost College is the campaign's newest confirmed program — launched NJCAA competition in 2023-24 under founding head coach and TSC/UTB alumnus Mario Zamora, who holds a genuine binational Mexican FA (FMF) and US Soccer coaching license — and is the only school in this batch on a real city campus (Brownsville, on the US-Mexico border), though it has no on-campus housing anywhere in the TSC system, unlike Paris JC, Jacksonville, and Northeast Texas CC, which all offer real on-campus dorms.

name: Northeast Conference
prestige: Mid-Major
mlsPipeline: Developing — NEC programs feed regional USL and NPSL pipelines
scholarships: NCAA D1 — up to 9.9 equivalencies (men's soccer); 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: Mercyhurst University (Erie, PA) — joined the NEC in Fall 2024; won the NEC regular-season title in that first D1 season
desc: The Northeast Conference is a mid-major D1 conference primarily located in the Northeast US corridor (NY, NJ, PA, CT, MD). Mercyhurst University joined the NEC in Fall 2024 — the program's first season at the NCAA D1 level after competing in D2 PSAC — and won the NEC regular-season title in that debut year. The conference spans from Long Island to Pittsburgh, with institutions ranging from 1,200 to 10,000 students. NEC soccer competes for an automatic NCAA Tournament bid each season.
olivierNote: Mercyhurst is the only NEC school in this guide, and it is stronger than its Fit Score implies: HC Austin Solomon won the NEC regular-season title in the program's first D1 season (2024) and his staff was named NEC Coaching Staff of the Year, before a fall to 8th in 2025. Note that Mercyhurst is a provisional D1 member and is not eligible for the NCAA championship postseason until 2028–29 — Olivier's first season (2027–28) sits inside that window. B.S. Exercise Science at Mercyhurst has a 500-hour clinical internship. Cost at ~$63k is offset by 93% of students receiving aid averaging $31k.

name: Summit League
prestige: Mid-major — Midwest/Plains base with East Coast men's soccer affiliates
mlsPipeline: Developing — Denver (departed to the WCC in 2026) drove the league's recent pipeline (Cole Bassett to USMNT, Shinyashiki = 2019 MLS Rookie of the Year)
scholarships: NCAA D1 — up to 9.9 equivalencies (men's soccer); 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: Delaware (Newark, DE) — joined for men's soccer in 2025; reached the 2025 Summit League semifinals
desc: The Summit League is an NCAA Division I conference founded in 1982 (as the Association of Mid-Continent Universities; renamed The Summit League in 2007), headquartered in Sioux Falls, SD, with a membership based in the Midwest and Plains. Six schools sponsor men's soccer: Kansas City, Omaha, Oral Roberts and St. Thomas, plus East Coast affiliates Delaware and UMass. Delaware joined in 2025 when its all-sports move to Conference USA left men's soccer without a home (CUSA does not sponsor the sport). Denver — five straight Summit titles 2021–2025 and a 2024 College Cup Final Four — departed for the West Coast Conference in 2026.
olivierNote: Delaware is the only Summit League school in this guide, filed here rather than under the CAA because its men's soccer competes in the Summit from 2025. Delaware is a strong value target — low ~$38k cost, a dedicated Kinesiology & Applied Physiology degree, a record-breaking 2025 (12-2-3, #24 nationally under HC Tommy McMenemy) and 25-minute access to the Philadelphia Union MLS ecosystem. Newark, DE is a classic college town but not a warm/city lifestyle match. Best-value East-Coast mid-major pick for Olivier.

name: Central Atlantic Collegiate Conference
prestige: Regional D2
mlsPipeline: Regional USL and NPSL pathway
scholarships: NCAA D2 — up to 9.0 equivalencies (men's soccer)
guideSchools: Georgian Court University (Lakewood, NJ) — Dino Raso, 2024 CACC Coach of the Year
desc: The Central Atlantic Collegiate Conference is a D2 conference primarily in the NY/NJ/PA/DE corridor. Georgian Court University (Lakewood, NJ) is the guide school — coach Dino Raso won the 2024 CACC Coach of the Year award, the first ever for GCU. The program runs a B.S. Exercise Science Wellness & Sports with explicit Pre-PT/OT/PA tracks.
olivierNote: Georgian Court is the CACC entry. Dino Raso (13th season, 2024 CACC Coach of Year) has built a consistent D2 program on the Jersey Shore. The Exercise Science Pre-PT track is one of the stronger academic offerings at this level. Jersey Shore beaches 20 min from campus, NYC 90 min north.

name: American Midwest Conference
prestige: NAIA
mlsPipeline: NAIA level — USL League Two pathway
scholarships: NAIA — 12 equivalencies, no per-player cap
guideSchools: Columbia College (Columbia, MO) — ⚠ No Exercise Science degree
desc: The American Midwest Conference is a NAIA conference primarily in Missouri, Iowa, and surrounding states. Columbia College (Columbia, MO) is the guide school — new coach Nathan Mason is rebuilding after significant roster turnover. ⚠ Columbia College does NOT offer Exercise Science — Healthcare Management and General Studies only.
olivierNote: ⚠ Columbia College MO is the value play — 7,556/yr sticker price with significant athletic aid potential. The degree limitation (no Exercise Science) is critical for a DPT-track student-athlete. Best as a cost-first option if Olivier plans to complete pre-req courses separately at nearby University of Missouri.

name: Patriot League
prestige: Mid-major — Midwest/Plains base with East Coast men's soccer affiliates
mlsPipeline: Developing — service academies and northeastern privates
scholarships: Army & Navy: full federal scholarships; other members: up to 9.9 equivalencies — 28 funded roster spots if House opt-in
guideSchools: Army West Point (West Point, NY) — men's soccer plays the Patriot League; full federal scholarship
Navy (Annapolis, MD) — men's soccer plays the Patriot League; full federal scholarship
desc: The Patriot League is an NCAA Division I conference of academically selective northeastern schools plus the Army and Navy service academies. It sponsors men's soccer with ten teams. Army West Point and Navy compete here for men's soccer even though their primary-athletics home for other sports is the American Athletic Conference (AAC) — an affiliate arrangement common to the service academies. Boston University, Bucknell and Colgate are the league's recent men's-soccer standard-bearers.
olivierNote: Army and Navy are filed under the Patriot League because that is where their men's soccer competes (not the AAC, where the guide previously listed them). Both offer a full federal scholarship — zero cost — but a mandatory military service commitment that is not compatible with Olivier's DPT/Chiropractic goal or an MLS pathway. Included for completeness and pipeline reference rather than as a target.
